subQuestions.questionText: The activity below (a person scuba diving in a shark cage) will be enjoyed by … tourists. (Refer to the image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
adventure
The shark cage diving activity shown is an adventure tourism activity.

subQuestions.questionText: Using insect repellent is a precaution against …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
malaria.
Insect repellent prevents mosquito bites which transmit malaria.

subQuestions.questionText: To apply for a …, tourists will visit the embassy of the country they intend to visit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
visa
A visa is applied for at the embassy of the country to be visited.

subQuestions.questionText: DST is applied by adjusting clocks …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
forward by one hour in summer.
Daylight Saving Time involves moving clocks forward by one hour during summer.

options.A: forward by one hour in winter.
options.B: backward by one hour in winter.
options.C: forward by one hour in summer.
options.D: backward by one hour in summer.

subQuestions.questionText: When it is 14:00 in Moscow (+3), the corresponding time in Cape Town is displayed on clock ... (Refer to the four clock images A, B, C, D in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
13:00
Cape Town is GMT+2, Moscow is GMT+3, so Cape Town is one hour behind Moscow. 14:00 - 1 hour = 13:00.

subQuestions.questionText: The daily increase and decrease in the value of a currency is known as …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
fluctuation.
Fluctuation refers to the daily changes in the value of a currency.

subQuestions.questionText: A strong performance of the rand against the US dollar may result in …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
fewer inbound tourists from USA.
A strong rand makes South Africa more expensive for US tourists, resulting in fewer inbound tourists from the USA.

options.C: no change in the number of visitors.
options.D: fewer outbound tourists to the USA.

subQuestions.questionText: A sought-after (desired) souvenir from a world-famous tourist region in Germany:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Cuckoo clock
Cuckoo clocks originate from the Black Forest region of Germany and are popular souvenirs.

subQuestions.questionText: A South African World Heritage Site associated with an object from space:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Vredefort Dome
The Vredefort Dome was created by a meteorite impact, making it associated with an object from space.

subQuestions.questionText: This icon is found in the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park in Australia:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Ayers Rock
Ayers Rock (also known as Uluru) is located in the Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park in Australia.

subQuestions.questionText: Tourists can visit this World Heritage Site by ferry:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
Robben Island
Robben Island is accessed by ferry from the V&A Waterfront in Cape Town.

subQuestions.questionText: Tourists to Canada may want to visit the …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Niagara Falls.
Niagara Falls is located on the border between Canada and the USA.

subQuestions.questionText: The organisation that collects global tourism statistics:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
UNWTO
UNWTO (United Nations World Tourism Organization) collects global tourism statistics.

subQuestions.questionText: The icon located in the harbour area of an Australian city:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
Sydney Opera House
The Sydney Opera House is located in Sydney Harbour, Australia.

subQuestions.questionText: Planting indigenous trees can be regarded as a/an … action.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (1 mark)
sustainable
Planting indigenous trees is a sustainable action that supports local ecosystems.

subQuestions.questionText: The business card below represents the … of a company. (Refer to the Sunshine Tours business card image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (1 mark)
professional image
A business card represents the professional image of a company.

subQuestions.questionText: This ultramarathon takes place in June annually:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Comrades
The Comrades Marathon is an annual ultramarathon held in June in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: The collapse of a building in George, a town in the Western Cape, is an example of …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (1 mark)
an unforeseen occurrence.
A building collapse is an unexpected, unforeseen event/occurrence.

subQuestions.questionText: The number of nights that tourists spend at a destination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
Length of stay
Length of stay refers to the duration tourists spend at a destination.

subQuestions.questionText: Responses to rate customer service can be collected using different methods. The method below (a printed rating form with checkboxes Excellent/Good/Average/Poor) is an example of a … (Refer to the image in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (1 mark)
feedback card.
A printed/handheld rating form with checkboxes is a feedback card.

subQuestions.questionText:
Give ONE word/term for the following description by choosing a word/term from the list below: preloaded foreign currency debit; SWIFT; cash; ATM; credit card; EFT.

Using a cellphone to pay for a product or service is an example of a/an … transaction.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: EFT (1 mark)
Using a cellphone to make payments is an Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) transaction.

subQuestions.questionText: Multiple currencies can be loaded onto a … card.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: preloaded foreign currency debit (1 mark)
A preloaded foreign currency debit card can hold multiple currencies.

subQuestions.questionText: A/An … can be used as payment when travelling overseas and is repaid in instalments to the bank.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: credit card (1 mark)
A credit card allows overseas payments to be made and repaid in instalments.

subQuestions.questionText: A backpacker from Brazil will use … to pay for souvenirs bought from street vendors in rural Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: cash (1 mark)
Street vendors in rural areas typically only accept cash payments.

subQuestions.questionText: A/An … transaction is used to do electronic money transfers between banks in different countries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: SWIFT (1 mark)
SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication) transactions are used for electronic money transfers between banks in different countries.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the correct word(s) from those given in brackets: People travelling at their own cost to assist with community projects are referred to as (sports tourists/voluntourists).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: voluntourists (1 mark)
Voluntourists travel at their own cost to volunteer/assist with community projects.

subQuestions.questionText: The main purpose of (FTT/ACSA) is to ensure that tourism businesses act fairly and responsibly.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: FTT (1 mark)
Fair Trade in Tourism (FTT) ensures tourism businesses act fairly and responsibly.

subQuestions.questionText: One way of reducing a carbon footprint is to (drive/cycle) to work.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: cycle (1 mark)
Cycling produces no carbon emissions, reducing the carbon footprint.

subQuestions.questionText: Collecting (rainwater/ivory) is considered to be a responsible practice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: rainwater (1 mark)
Collecting rainwater is a sustainable, responsible practice that conserves water.

subQuestions.questionText: (Solar/Coal) is an example of a non-renewable energy source.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Coal (1 mark)
Coal is a fossil fuel and a non-renewable energy source.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the host city (cities) from COLUMN B that match(es) the travel trade show in COLUMN A. Write only the letter (A–F) next to the question numbers (1.4.1 to 1.4.5).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
1.4.1 D / London
1.4.2 E / Berlin
1.4.3 B / Cape Town and Johannesburg (also accept F / Cape Town)
1.4.4 A / Durban
1.4.5 F / Cape Town

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the photograph collage 'OUR WORLD TOURS' showing six tourist attractions. Write down the number of countries Jake's grandparents visited.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Four (1 mark)
The collage shows attractions from 4 different countries: Germany (Black Forest), Italy (Leaning Tower of Pisa, Venice — same country), Egypt (Pyramids/Sphinx), Brazil (Christ the Redeemer).

subQuestions.questionText: Name the icons located in the same European country they visited.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (1 mark each):
Leaning Tower of Pisa AND Venice (both located in Italy)
[Award 2 marks for naming both icons correctly.]

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the icon they visited, which is located in the Southern Hemisphere.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Statue of Christ the Redeemer (1 mark)
Located in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil — in the Southern Hemisphere.

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE icon located on the African continent.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 1 mark):
The Great Pyramids of Giza
OR
The Sphinx
(Both located in Egypt, Africa.)

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'TOKYO, JAPAN – DID YOU KNOW?' infographic showing six attractions: Disneyland, Capital City (sushi), Mount Fuji, Shibuya Crossing, Cherry Blossoms, and Tokyo Skytree.

A South African couple, David and his wife Claire, visited their son and his family in Tokyo. They were excited to see their two grandchildren, aged 4 and 6 years old. Before departure, they compiled an itinerary including the attractions in the infographic.

Redraw and complete the table in your ANSWER BOOK by suggesting activities for Days 3, 4, 5 and 6:
Day 1: Arrival in Tokyo
Day 2: At leisure
Day 3: Activity to expose children to marine life
Day 4: Activity suitable for adults
Day 5: Opportunity to meet movie characters
Day 6: Enjoy the local cuisine
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
Day 3: Visit the Skytree and the aquarium / Visit the aquarium / Visit the Skytree / Visit the tallest building
Day 4: Hike / climb Mount Fuji / Experience the Shibuya crossing
Day 5: Visit Tokyo Disneyland
Day 6: Eat Sushi / Eat Japanese food
[Award 1 mark per correct, age/audience-appropriate suggestion.]

subQuestions.questionText:
David and Claire departed from OR Tambo International Airport at 16:00 on 6 May 2025. The duration of the flight from Johannesburg to Tokyo was 19 hours.

Calculate the time and date the couple arrived in Tokyo.

NOTE: Japan does NOT practise DST.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Johannesburg +2; Tokyo +9 (identifying time zones)
Mark 2: Time difference = 7 hours
Mark 3: Departure time from Johannesburg = 16:00
Mark 4: Local time in Tokyo at departure = 16:00 + 7 hours = 23:00 (6 May 2025)
Mark 5: Flying time added = 23:00 + 19 hours
Mark 6: Arrival time in Tokyo = 18:00 on 7 May 2025

Final answer: 18:00 on 7 May 2025
[Award full 6 marks for the answer 18:00 on 7 May 2025 if working is shown.]

subQuestions.questionText:
The couple landed safely at Tokyo International Airport.

Explain ONE way in which the couple kept their luggage safe while waiting at the airport.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• They did not leave their luggage unattended.
• Did not allow strangers to look after the luggage.
• Made use of registered airport porter services to assist with luggage.
• Used a lock-up facility / luggage storage facility.
[Award 2 marks for a clear explanation of one way to keep luggage safe.]

subQuestions.questionText:
As South Africans, the couple did not need a visa for their trip to Japan. They were allowed to enjoy a 'visa-free' holiday for up to 90 days.

Name ONE compulsory entry document the couple needed for their trip to Japan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): Valid passport
NOTE: Answer MUST include the word 'valid' to receive full marks.

subQuestions.questionText: Name the government department where the couple had to apply for the document named in QUESTION 2.4.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): Department of Home Affairs
• Also accept: Home Affairs

subQuestions.questionText:
The couple was extremely tired and disorientated on arrival in Tokyo.

Name the travel-related condition they suffered from.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (2 marks): Jet lag

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.5.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
The couple crossed many time zones (seven time zones) during their flight.
[Award 2 marks for clear reasoning linking jet lag to crossing multiple time zones.]

subQuestions.questionText: Besides the above-mentioned symptoms, name TWO other symptoms of the identified condition.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Headaches
• Disturbed sleeping patterns
• Diarrhea
• Swollen legs and feet
• Vomiting
• Lack of appetite
• Dizziness
• Dehydration
[Award 2 marks per correctly identified symptom.]

subQuestions.questionText:
The Shibuya Crossing is the busiest pedestrian crossing in Tokyo.

Suggest TWO ways how tourists could stay safe when walking in the streets of Tokyo.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Do not ask strangers for direction or assistance.
• Do not display expensive items such as cellphones, video cameras or jewellery.
• Leave original travel documents in a safe place.
• Do not carry large amounts of cash.
• Adhere to road signs.
• Do not wander off into deserted/isolated areas.
• Take legally permitted self-defense gadgets when walking in the streets.
• Stay alert.
[Award 2 marks per correctly explained safety tip.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Discuss how the family could prepare themselves for the activity on Day 5 (Visit Tokyo Disneyland).

Preparations BEFORE the activity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Do research on Tokyo Disneyland.
• Book entry tickets in advance to avoid queues.
• Consider weather conditions beforehand in order to dress appropriately.
• Ensure that electronic devices are charged.
• Organise transport to and from Tokyo Disneyland.
[Award 2 marks for a clear preparation suggestion.]

subQuestions.questionText: Preparations FOR the actual activity (Day 5 — Tokyo Disneyland visit).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Have digital entry tickets readily available.
• Ensure communication amongst the group.
• Maximise the time spent at Tokyo Disneyland.
• Dress comfortably.
• Take preventative measures against adverse weather conditions.
[Award 2 marks per correctly explained preparation point.]

subQuestions.questionText:
David wanted to bring a small cherry blossom tree from Japan to plant in his garden.

Was David allowed to bring the cherry blossom tree into South Africa? Give ONE reason for your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: No (no mark for No alone)

Reason (2 marks):
• David does not have the required permit or authorisation to bring plants into South Africa.
• Custom regulations stipulate that no plants or plant products may be brought into South Africa without an import permit from the National Plant Protection Organisation of South Africa (NPPOZA).

NOTE: Do NOT award marks for YES/NO alone — full 2 marks awarded only for the reason.

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the exchange rate table:
| Country | Currency Code | BBR | BSR |
| USA | USD | 18,42 | 18,65 |
| Japan | JPY | 0,12 | 0,14 |
| England | GBP | 23,29 | 23,30 |

Name the currency used in Japan.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): Yen
• Also accept: Japanese Yen
NOTE: Do NOT accept the symbol (¥) or currency code JPY.

subQuestions.questionText:
David had R68 000 to spend while he was in Japan. He exchanged his money for the Japanese currency at OR Tambo International Airport before departure.

Calculate the amount he received in the Japanese currency. (Round off to TWO decimal places.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identify correct rate to use — Bank Selling Rate (BSR) = 0,14 (since David is buying foreign currency)
Mark 2: Calculation: R68 000 ÷ 0,14
Mark 3: Final answer: ¥485 714,29

Final answer: ¥485 714,29
[Award full 3 marks for correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:
A day trip to Mount Fuji costs ¥10 820 PER PERSON.

Calculate the equivalent of this amount in ZAR for the COUPLE. (Round off to TWO decimal places.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Use Bank Buying Rate (BBR) = 0,12 (since converting yen back to ZAR)
Mark 2: Calculation per person: ¥10 820 × 0,12
Mark 3: = R1 298,40 per person
Mark 4: Multiply by 2 (for the couple): R1 298,40 × 2
Mark 5: Final answer: R2 596,80

Final answer: R2 596,80
[Award full 5 marks for correct final answer with valid working.]

subQuestions.questionText:
The money spent by tourists sets the multiplier effect into motion.

Explain TWO ways how the multiplier effect benefits the local communities around Mount Fuji.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• The money spent by the tourists is used to pay the salaries of the staff working at the mountain.
• The staff will spend the money in their communities thus ensuring a better standard of living.
• Visitors will buy souvenirs made by the local people – money flows back into the local community.
• Entrepreneurial opportunities are created for the supply of local products and services.
• Creation of job opportunities/skills development for the local community.
• The money generated by tourism can be used towards conservation efforts to protect the mountain for future generations.
• Improved infrastructure / Development of new infrastructure.
• Local economic growth.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained way the multiplier effect benefits locals.]

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to 'THE HEART OF ROME — THE VATICAN CITY – THE WORLD'S SMALLEST COUNTRY' image.

Name the country where the Vatican City is located.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (1 mark): Italy

subQuestions.label: 4.1.1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Name the continent where the Vatican City is found.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (1 mark): Europe

subQuestions.questionText: Name the religious head of the Vatican City.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): The Pope
• Also accept: Pope Francis / Pope Leo XIV
• The Pope of the Catholic Church
• The leader of the Catholic Church

subQuestions.questionText: List THREE sites within the Vatican City that are popular tourist attractions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any THREE — 2 marks each):
• St. Peter's Basilica
• Saint Peter's Square
• The Vatican Museums
• Chapels e.g. the Sistine Chapel
• Catholic Cathedrals
• Catholic Church
• Vatican Library and Museum
[Award 2 marks per correctly listed site.]

subQuestions.questionText:
The Sistine Chapel is located within the Vatican Museum.

Explain TWO reasons why tourists will visit the Sistine Chapel.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel is one of the most famous artworks in the world, painted by Michelangelo.
• It took Michelangelo approximately four years to paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
• The painted ceiling of the Sistine Chapel is considered one of the most celebrated masterpieces in the history of art.
• Chapel where the election of a new pontiff/pope takes place.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained reason.]

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between the Vatican City as a tourist destination and a religious site.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (2 marks each):
Tourist destination (2 marks): The Vatican City attracts tourists from around the world contributing to the city's economy through tourism related activities (e.g. attractions, art, history, museums).

Religious site (2 marks): Religious tourists belonging to this faith will see the visit as a pilgrimage with the hope of seeing the Pope.

[Award 2 marks for each clear differentiation point.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to images A and B labelled 'FAMOUS WALLS OF THE WORLD'.
Identify icons A and B above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
A: Great Wall of China
B: Berlin Wall

subQuestions.questionText:
The walls above are located on different continents.

Name the TWO continents where the walls are located.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
• Asia (for Great Wall of China)
• Europe (for Berlin Wall)
NOTE: Accept any order.

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the purpose of constructing EACH of the walls, A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (2 marks each):
A — Great Wall of China (2 marks): The Great Wall of China was constructed to protect China from invasions by other tribes.

B — Berlin Wall (2 marks): The Berlin Wall was constructed to separate East and West Berlin during the Cold War era.
• Also accept: The Berlin Wall was constructed to separate communism and democracy/capitalism.
• Both walls were built to separate territories and people.

NOTE: The responses MUST include information on BOTH walls (A and B).
[Award 2 marks per correct purpose for each wall.]

subQuestions.questionText:
In order to be regarded as successful, tourist attractions must consider people with special needs.

Write a paragraph to explain how attractions can ensure UNIVERSAL ACCESS for tourists with special needs.

Your paragraph must include the following:
• An explanation of the term universal access (2)
• TWO examples of how universal access will assist tourists with special needs (4)
subQuestions.memoText:
Universal Access — Explanation (2 marks):
• Making sure everyone can use a service or facility, regardless of their physical abilities, age or background.
• To ensure inclusivity and equal opportunities for all.
[Award 2 marks for a clear explanation of universal access.]

Examples (any TWO — 2 marks each, total 4 marks):
• Provide accessible facilities.
• Having ramps and lifts for people in wheelchairs.
• Offering audio guides or braille information for visitors who are visually impaired.
• Providing accessible bathrooms and seating areas for people with mobility issues.
• Designing pathways and trails with smooth surfaces and gentle slopes for people using walkers or canes.
• Offering sign language interpretation for individuals who have a hearing impairment.
• Providing tactile experiences or virtual tours for visitors with sensory impairments.
• Guide dogs.
• Bathrooms with baby nappy-changing facilities.
• Trained staff to assist tourists with special needs.

NOTE: Accept examples relevant to universal access.
[Total: 6 marks]

questions.title: Culture and Heritage Tourism — South Africa's World Heritage Sites

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the map of South Africa showing the approximate location of FIVE of South Africa's World Heritage Sites labelled A, B, C, D and E.
(A: in Gauteng, B: in Northern Cape on west coast, C: in northern KwaZulu-Natal near Hluhluwe, D: near Cape Town, E: along the Lesotho border in KZN/EC.)

Identify the World Heritage Sites labelled A, B, C, D and E on the map. Write the letters A, B, C, D and E with the full names of the World Heritage Sites in the ANSWER BOOK.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (2 marks each):
A: Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa (2 marks)
B: Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape (2 marks)
C: iSimangaliso Wetland Park (2 marks)
D: Robben Island (2 marks)
E: Maloti-Drakensberg Park (2 marks)

[Award 2 marks per correctly identified World Heritage Site at the indicated map location. Total: 10 marks.]

questions.title: Marketing — Trevor Noah Markets South Africa

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'TREVOR NOAH MARKETS SOUTH AFRICA' extract — Trevor Noah was invited by the TBCSA to appear in a marketing video.

Write the acronym TBCSA in full.
subQuestions.memoText: Expected answer (2 marks): Tourism Business Council of South Africa

subQuestions.questionText:
The TBCSA used Trevor Noah to promote our beautiful country.

Give ONE reason why Trevor Noah was an ideal choice to market South Africa locally, in the USA and in other countries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• He is a South African with a huge following in both his home country, the USA and in other countries.
• Due to his popularity and fame the video will reach a wide audience.
• People will enjoy his humour in the video and will share the video worldwide.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, valid reason.]

subQuestions.questionText:
SATourism is responsible for creating international awareness of South Africa as a travel destination.

State TWO other marketing roles of SATourism.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Maintaining and enhancing the standard of facilities and services for tourists.
• Coordinating the marketing activities of role players in the industry.
• Creating opportunities for marketing SA internationally: ITB (Berlin), World Travel Market (London).
[Award 2 marks per correctly stated marketing role.]

questions.title: Tourism Sectors — Professional Image and Conditions of Employment

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'PROFESSIONAL IMAGE' infographic showing six aspects: Appearance, Communication, Teamwork, Customer Service, Punctuality, Professional Behaviour.

Give ONE reason why it is important to maintain a professional appearance when working in the tourism industry.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
Dressing neatly and maintaining good grooming and personal hygiene show professionalism and respect for customers, colleagues and the business.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, well-explained reason.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Good communication is vital in the tourism industry.

Discuss ONE consequence (effect) if an employee working in the tourism industry is unable to communicate clearly.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Poor communication can lead to misunderstanding and potential conflicts.
• Messages may be misinterpreted and can lead to confusion.
• Poor communication can negatively impact on the performance of an employee.
• Can negatively impact the business.
[Award 2 marks for a fully discussed consequence.]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO ways in which effective teamwork can contribute to the professional image of a business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• Teamwork is vital in tourism, as many professionals work together to serve customers or handle tasks.
• It improves efficiency and ensures a smooth and enjoyable experience for the customers.
• It ensures better coordination in delivering a seamless service/experience.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained way teamwork builds professional image.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT' extract about Sarah, a park ranger at the Kruger National Park.

Identify Sarah's main responsibility as a park ranger.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Ensure visitor safety
• Do park patrols
• Report incidents or safety hazards to supervisors
[Award 2 marks for a clearly identified main responsibility from the extract.]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why employees of the Kruger National Park should follow a code of conduct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
• It informs employees about what behaviour and performance is expected.
• It encourages ethical and responsible actions.
• It treats all employees fairly and equally.
• It fosters honesty and integrity between customers and colleagues.
• It helps prevent misconduct and legal issues.
• It creates a positive and respectful workplace.
• It helps employees make the right choices in tough situations.
• It ensures the park follows laws and regulations to ensure the safety of visitors to the park.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained reason.]

subQuestions.questionText: Give the regular working hours per week as stipulated in the BCEA (Basic Conditions of Employment Act, 1997 (Act 75 of 1997)).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks): 45 hours per week
• Also accept: 9 hours per day

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to Sarah's contract of employment which stipulates: a uniform allowance of R400 a month, twenty leave days per year, access to the park facilities for personal use, and a notice period for termination.

Complete the sentence by filling in the missing word.
Sarah has access to the Kruger National Park's facilities for personal use. This is regarded as a … benefit.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (1 mark): fringe
('Fringe benefit' = a non-wage benefit given to employees in addition to their normal salary.)

subQuestions.questionText:
According to the BCEA, a notice period is required before an employee may terminate (end) his/her service.

Explain the term notice period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (2 marks):
The period of time an employee must give the employer before leaving a job.
[Award 2 marks for a clear, accurate explanation of notice period.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Sarah receives a uniform allowance.

Give ONE reason why a park ranger needs to wear a uniform when on duty.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):
• Uniforms make park rangers easily identifiable to visitors.
• Uniforms ensure visitors know who to approach for assistance.
• Complete uniforms often include gear that ensures the ranger's safety while performing their duties.
• It helps maintain a neat and professional look, which is important for public interactions.
• The style and colour of a park ranger's uniform are appropriate for the type of work they perform daily.
[Award 2 marks for a clearly explained reason.]

questions.title: Sustainable and Responsible Tourism — Conduct for Responsible Tourists

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the 'CONDUCT FOR RESPONSIBLE TOURISTS' extract addressing: Value local traditions and customs, Support the local economy, and Respect the environment.

The code of conduct above addresses the three pillars of sustainability.
Name the THREE pillars.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (1 mark each):
• Economic / Profit
• Social / People
• Environmental / Planet
[Award 1 mark per correctly named pillar.]

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why it is important to buy products that do not harm endangered plants or animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (any ONE — 2 marks):

• Preserves biodiversity and protects ecosystems.
• It can help support conservation efforts thereby promoting sustainability.
[Award 2 marks for a clear conservation-focused reason.]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO reasons why it is important to ask permission of the local people before taking photos of them.
subQuestions.memoText:

• It ensures that personal boundaries are respected.
• It ensures that locals grant permission before their photos are taken.
• It could have legal implications if photos are taken without permission.
[Award 2 marks per fully explained reason.]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO impacts of the Russian-Ukraine conflict on the economy of Ukraine.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answers (any TWO — 2 marks each):
